title: The version of my strategy with the highest win rate was the only one that lost money
author: person-person12
selftext:
I ran the same opening range breakout on QQQ 5 minute candles from jan 2020 to dec 2025. 116,677 candles, about 1,057 trades per run, 100k account. Same entry, same stop, same session cutoff. **The only thing I moved was the target.**

**1:1 target** ... 54.54% win rate, profit factor 0.99, net **-2.30%**, max drawdown 22.2%

**1:2 target** ... 48.34% win rate, profit factor 1.03, net +6.96%, max drawdown 24.41%

**1:3 target** ... 47.73% win rate, profit factor 1.04, net +9.96%, max drawdown 24.34%

The version that won most often is the one that finished red. It won six percentage points more of its trades than the 1:3 and still gave money back, because a 1:1 winner only ever pays for one loser and it had 481 of them.

The part I didnt expect was the second number underneath it. That 1:1 run made **+14.94% before costs and -2.30% after them.** Commission and slippage came to **$17,237** across 1,058 trades. So the whole outcome of that version was the execution bill, and I only saw it because [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) charges both sides by default instead of handing me the clean number first.

Its a bit like selling out your whole stall at the market and still going home short because the pitch fee took the margin. The number on the sign was never the one deciding anything.

1:3 is not free either. It holds positions longer, its drawdown was 24.34% against 22.2%, and it hands back a pile of trades that were green at 1R and closed at the session cutoff for less. Somebody who needs a smooth daily curve would genuinely rather have the 1:1 shape and it would genuinely cost them money.

All three runs sit on the same 116,677 candles, so the target is the only thing that differs between them.

comments.author: HereForTheCharts
comments.body:
Win rate alone can definitely be misleading   
The fees slippage part is eye opening

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Yea the fees part gets me every time. On a 3 year NQ run I did the commission and slippage bill came to about **89k against a 153% net return**, so over a third of the gross result went to costs before I looked at anything else. What are you paying per round turn?
